title: perf:chores fails its 50 ms long-task budget on one run in two under load
body:
## Summary
The perf gate judges the long-task budget on a single run, and `pnpm perf:chores` (fresh build each time) failed it 4 times in 8 this session with one 52-63 ms task, while the same build re-driven passed 9 of 9.

## Description
`apps/desktop/scripts/perf-budgets.mjs:340` takes the longest task over one run and `:356` fails it above 50 ms (ADR 0089, docs/redesign/fathom.md section 5: "Long tasks during a transition: 0 over 50 ms"). `apps/desktop/scripts/perf-gate.mjs` runs each scene once. Measured on 2026-10-16 with sibling agents running (25-26 node processes): perf:chores with its own `vite build` first failed at 54, 63, 52 and 55 ms (the last inside the old chained perf:all, which then never judged mind) and passed 4 times at 0; the same dist-perf driven by the old and the new drive alternately (`--url`), 6 runs, and 3 more runs against freshly started preview servers, all gave 0 ms; the one-build `perf:all --all` passed chores at 0 twice. So the red tracks the minutes right after a build on a loaded machine, not the scene. The technique measurement-honesty/noise-band-and-hysteresis says a verdict near its threshold needs a band or a repeat, and quality-gates/blocking-by-input-determinism says a blocking check must not vary on an uncontrolled input. The budget itself must not be loosened (ADR 0089: a budget changes only by a later ADR); what is missing is the attribution of the task to a step and a repeat rule.

## Flow
- pnpm perf:chores -> vite build -> preview -> Edge drives the chores path once -> longest long task 52-63 ms in 4 of 8 runs -> FAIL
- the fix, in order: record each long task's startTime against the drive's step marks (the wrapper in the round's scratch probe did this) so a red names its step; run 10 times with and without the preceding build; then decide in an ADR between a best-of-N or median rule and a fixed warm-up, never a higher threshold

## Expected impact
Whoever runs perf:all (the director, the cutover hand pass) stops seeing a red that is the machine's; a real long task in a step is then named, not guessed. What could break: a repeat rule that hides a real intermittent 60 ms task in the scene.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the gate's verdict on chores is the scene's, not the machine's load
Before: perf:chores fresh-build runs: 4 of 8 FAIL (52, 54, 55, 63 ms); same-build re-drives 9 of 9 at 0 ms
After: not measured: the instrument (step attribution plus a 10-run distribution) is unbuilt
Method: experiment - the A/B re-drives above; the gate rule itself is not changed, so no After
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: a drive wrapper that records PerformanceObserver longtask startTime against page.keyboard/click marks, run 10x via pnpm perf:chores and 10x on a warm build

title: The lightbox covers the depth frame, not the window: the stage chrome stays live
body:
## Summary
The chores lightbox is `position: fixed; inset: 0` inside `.pa-page`, whose `container-type: inline-size` makes it the containing block, so the scrim covers 1600x788 of a 1600x900 window and the stage's top band and dock stay uncovered and pressable.

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/chores.css:999` `.lbx { position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 60 }` renders inside `.pa-page` (`apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/topic.tsx` returns it in the page), and `.pa-page` sets `container-type: inline-size` (`chores.css:27`), which applies layout containment, and a layout-contained box is the containing block of its fixed descendants. Measured in Edge on the built preview: `.lbx` rect [0,36,1600,788], `.pa-page` rect [0,36,1600,788], viewport 1600x900. The file's own words claim otherwise: `lightbox.tsx:4` "A still opened over everything" and `chores.css.test.ts:84` "the lightbox covers everything" (the test checks the declarations, not the box). modal-stack/layering-and-precedence: an overlay must rank over the shell it claims to cover. The fix is a portal to `document.body` (or a stage-level overlay slot), which changes stacking against the stage's own layers and must be looked at in the real window.

## Flow
- open a chore's topic -> press a still -> the scrim and still cover the depth frame only -> the top band (36 px) and the dock (Athena, Depths) stay visible and clickable
- the fix: render the lightbox through createPortal into document.body, keep focus return and the Tab wrap (7cbacb0), give it the overlay z band, and re-run the rect probe

## Expected impact
The person sees a still that is modal everywhere but the dock they can still press, which moves the scene under an open dialog. Measured by the probe's rect against the viewport. Could break: stacking against the stage layers or the companion window chrome.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the modal still covers the window it claims to
Before: lightbox rect 1600x788 at y=36 in a 1600x900 viewport (Edge, built preview)
After: not measured: a portal needs the stage's z bands checked in the real window
Method: simulation - the Before is a probe; the After needs the change seen against the stage chrome
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: the round's lightbox rect probe (playwright-core over vite preview of dist-perf): .lbx getBoundingClientRect against innerWidth/innerHeight, then a look in the Tauri window

title: Copy and Start for real say they worked whether or not the act succeeded
body:
## Summary
The topic page says "Sent the command to the clipboard." and the studio's showcase says "Handed to her with your case" unconditionally; the module's copy and hand return nothing and log a failure to the console only.

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/topic.tsx` Copy the command calls `model.actions.copy(p.command)` then `setSaid("Sent the command to the clipboard.")`; `apps/desktop/src/modules/playbooks/index.ts:18-27` `copy` is `void navigator.clipboard?.writeText(text).catch(console.error)` (with no clipboard it does nothing at all) and `hand` is `void athenaOffer(...).catch(console.error)`. `apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/adopt/studio.tsx:233-238` calls hand then `setHanded(true)`, and `adopt/showcase.tsx:112-116` then says it waits in her composer. The copy-auditor's second defect class: a message that names an outcome that did not happen. The fix needs `PlaybookActions.copy` and `.hand` to return a Promise the scene awaits (`apps/desktop/src/modules/playbooks/model.ts:36`), which is the desktop-playbooks module's file, outside this round.

## Flow
- Copy the command with clipboard permission denied -> writeText rejects -> console.error only -> the page says Sent the command to the clipboard
- Start for real with her window down -> athenaOffer rejects -> console only -> the showcase says Handed to her
- the fix: copy and hand return Promise<void>; topic and studio say the success line on resolve and a ProblemNote-style line on reject

## Expected impact
The person who pastes nothing, or waits for a composer that never got the command, is told the opposite. A wired test with a rejecting copy/hand spy measures it. Could break: callers that ignore the returned promise (lint catches floating promises).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the status line reports the act's real outcome
Before: 3 of 3 walked cases (clipboard missing, writeText rejected, athenaOffer rejected) show the success line
After: 0 of 3, predicted, once copy/hand return their promise and the scene awaits it
Method: simulation - walked from the code; the fix starts in modules/playbooks, out of this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: contract
instrument: wired.test.tsx and studio.test.tsx cases with copy/hand spies that reject, asserting the failure line instead of the success line

title: The replay's turn is a live region mounted fresh at every step
body:
## Summary
`TurnView` is `aria-live="polite"`, but the replay remounts at every step (a new layer per move, and `key={at}`), so the region arrives already full; whether a screen reader reads each turn, reads nothing, or reads the whole turn is unverified.

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/turn.tsx:30` puts `aria-live="polite"` on the article; `apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/replay.tsx:234` keys it by `at`, and each step is a move (`replay.tsx:99`), which the stage renders as a new layer. A live region announces changes to a region already in the tree; one inserted with its content is announced inconsistently across screen readers, and when it is, the whole turn (the person's words, hers, the reads, every card) is read at each step, also while Play runs every 2.8 s. The same view is used by the studio's showcase. The fix is a persistent, terse live line at the scene level ("Turn 4 of 12, Carrier billing centre, filed") and no live attribute on the article; deciding that it reads well needs NVDA or Narrator in the real window.

## Flow
- a screen-reader user presses ArrowRight in the replay -> a new layer mounts with a new aria-live article -> announcement depends on the reader
- Play -> every 2.8 s a new full article -> either silence or the whole turn read over the last

## Expected impact
Screen-reader users of the replay. Measured only with a reader. Could break: nothing visible.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - each step is announced once, briefly
Before: unknown: no screen reader was available to this round
After: unknown
Method: simulation - the DOM is certain, the announcement is not; jsdom cannot speak
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/turn.tsx:30 aria-live="polite"
apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/replay.tsx:234 <TurnView key={at} turn={t} at={at} total={trace.length} />
apps/desktop/src/stage/Stage.tsx:195 key={l.key} (a fresh layer per move)

title: The studio and the front door each keep their own copy of the reconnect loop
body:
## Summary
`adopt/session.ts` and `intake/session.ts` both implement follow-from-last-seq with 1/2/4 s backoff and five tries as two forty-line loops; only the constants and `why` are shared.

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/adopt/session.ts:82-126` and `apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/intake/session.ts:52-98` are the same loop (events from `seq.current`, reset `tries` on any event, closed on SESSION_CLOSED, `retrying` then `lost` after MAX_TRIES, the `realWait` backoff), and the intake one adds a verdict stop. `intake/session.ts:19` imports `BACKOFF_MS, MAX_TRIES, why` from the adopt session, so the rule is half shared: a fix to the loop's behaviour (when an event resets the count, what a clean end of stream means) must be made twice, which is the parity-auditor's class. The fix: one `followSession(client, id, seq, signal, dispatch, stopOn)` used by both hooks, with a contract test that drives both through one dropping scripted client.

## Flow
- a stream drops in the studio -> adopt loop retries; the same drop at the front door -> the intake loop, identical today
- the fix: extract the loop, keep both hooks' tests green, add one shared case per transition (event resets tries, clean end retries, closed stops, sixth failure is lost)

## Expected impact
The next change to reconnect behaviour lands once. Measured as duplicated loop sites 2 -> 1 with both suites green. Could break: the verdict stop and the closed stop ordering.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one implementation of the reconnect rule
Before: 2 loops, ~40 lines each, same transitions
After: 1 loop, 2 callers (predicted)
Method: simulation - read side by side; the extraction is M with risk 4, past this round's Lane A
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a shared contract test running useAdoptSession and useIntakeSession against one scripted client that drops, ends cleanly and closes

title: fathom.md describes a perf gate with a dev server, screenshots and 12 budgets
body:
## Summary
docs/redesign/fathom.md section 7 says the gate runs from the shell's dev server, writes its numbers next to screenshots and fails on any section 5 budget; the gate serves a production preview, prints to stdout, takes no screenshot and measures 5 of the 12 rows.

## Description
`docs/redesign/fathom.md:157-161`: "run from the shell's own dev server", "writes the numbers next to the screenshots", "fails the run when a budget in section 5 is missed". `apps/desktop/scripts/perf-gate.mjs:128-153` builds and serves `vite preview` on purpose (its comment: a production bundle, not the dev server), `show()` only console.logs, and `perf-budgets.mjs:BUDGETS` judges frame p95, dropped share, long task, loops per frame and idle requests; section 5's React renders per frame, cold chrome under 300 ms, scenes mounted and the property rule are not measured by it (first-paint JS is held by console/graph.test.ts). Section 5's "no frame callbacks when nothing is moving" is `idleFrameRequests: 2` in the code. quality-gates/prose-rule-drift: a documented rule a reader trusts and no check holds. The doc is under docs/, outside this round.

## Flow
- a reader of fathom.md looks for the screenshots and numbers file -> none exists; believes React renders per frame are gated -> nothing measures them
- the fix: rewrite section 7's bullet to what the gate does, list which section 5 rows it measures and which other test holds each of the rest, and state the idle tolerance of 2

## Expected impact
Whoever trusts the design doc for what is gated. Measured as doc claims contradicted by the code: 3 + the 7 unmeasured rows -> 0. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the design doc states the gate the code runs
Before: 3 false claims in section 7, 7 of 12 section 5 rows named as gated with no gate
After: 0 (predicted)
Method: probe - each claim checked against perf-gate.mjs and perf-budgets.mjs; the doc is out of scope
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
docs/redesign/fathom.md:157 - `scripts/perf-gate.mjs` (Playwright, run from the shell's own dev server): drives the same path
docs/redesign/fathom.md:160 idle window. It fails the run when a budget in section 5 is missed and writes the numbers next to the
apps/desktop/scripts/perf-gate.mjs:130 spawnSync("pnpm exec vite build --outDir dist-perf --emptyOutDir"
apps/desktop/scripts/perf-budgets.mjs:311 idleFrameRequests: 2,
instrument: the claim-by-claim check above, re-run against the edited section

title: No perf drive enters the Adopt studio's conversation or the New chore front door
body:
## Summary
The two chores levels with streaming feeds and timers (the studio's scripted session, the front door's) are outside every perf budget: the chores drive uses the shipped fixture, whose studio is the no-daemon note.

## Description
`apps/desktop/scripts/perf-chores.drive.mjs` drives `&fixture=shipped`, where `adoptDepsFor` (`apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/adopt/fixtures.ts:625`) returns undefined, so the studio draws only its ProblemNote; nothing presses New chore. The `adopt` and `intake-template` fixtures play scripted sessions with timers and a growing feed (`adopt/fixtures.ts`, `intake/fixtures.ts:123`), which is where per-frame work or an idle timer would hide. `perf-gate.mjs` maps one scene name to one drive (`scripts/perf-<scene>.drive.mjs`), so a second chores scenario needs a naming rule (for example `perf-chores-adopt.drive.mjs` with its own query) and the `drivesIn` pattern widened.

## Flow
- pnpm perf:all -> chores studio visited only as its no-daemon note -> a timer left running in the scripted conversation would never be seen
- the fix: a drive over `?scene=chores&fixture=adopt` (answer two cards, Good enough, approve, watch the showcase, Close) and one over intake-template; allow `perf-<scene>-<variant>.drive.mjs` in drivesIn and the parity test

## Expected impact
The conversation surfaces get the same idle and long-task budgets as the rest. Measured by the new drives' first runs. Could break: a red on first run that is the scripted fixture's own timer.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every chores level is under the budgets
Before: 0 of 2 conversation levels driven
After: 2 of 2 (predicted)
Method: simulation - the drives do not exist yet
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: two new drives run through perf-gate --scene; their numbers are the After

title: The sheet says only transform and opacity move, and eases colour on nine hovers
body:
## Summary
chores.css's header (and the overlay's rule) says only transform and opacity animate, while nine rules ease color, background or border-color on hover and the sheet's own test requires a hover transition on every pressable control.

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/chores.css:3-4` "Motion is `transform` and `opacity` and nothing else"; the overlay's rules say "Animate transform and opacity only". Yet `chores.css:94, 157, 192, 265, 407, 862, 1049, 1279, 1425` transition `color`, `background` or `border-color` on `--duration-fast`, `chores.css.test.ts:31` demands a transition on every `cursor: pointer` rule, and app.css itself eases colour in 5 rules. Either hover colour fades are an exemption the rule should name (ADR 0089 is about moves, layers and per-frame work), or they are violations across the app. That is a policy call for the owner, not a sweep's.

## Flow
- a reader holds the sheet to its header -> nine violations; holds it to its test -> nine compliances
- the decision: name hover colour fades on --duration-fast as allowed in ADR 0089's rule (and the header), or migrate them to opacity washes app-wide

## Expected impact
Future sweeps stop reading one rule two ways. Could break: nothing until the call is made.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one stated motion rule that the code and its tests agree with
Before: rule text: transform/opacity only; code: 9 colour transitions in this sheet, 5 in app.css; test: requires them
After: depends on the call
Method: probe - grep of transition declarations; the outcome is a policy decision
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/chores.css:3 * Tokens and mixes of them only. Nothing under 12px; reading text 14px and up. Motion is
apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/chores.css:94 transition:
apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/chores.css.test.ts:31 test("every control the pointer can press eases its hover on the fast duration"
